modules/shell/MODULE.md:30:`registry` maps a fixed key to its Tenant: a Script whose `static create(deps) -> {ok, value: Control, error}` builds it, or a Callable with the same signature. The Tenant is created on the Tab's first show (`deps = {"key": key}`) and added to that Tab's Page, a plain white surface; a key with no entry keeps the white Page (`tenant_state` says `shell.tenant_missing`); a `create` that fails leaves it white and records `shell.tenant_failed`. The Shell's show/hide rule (ticket #24): the visible Page runs; once a fade has settled every hidden Page is `visible = false`, `process_mode DISABLED` (no `_process`, no input callbacks, no tweens, no video) with any focus inside it released, and resumes with its state intact from the moment its fade-in starts.

Changed from the prototype: the paintbox reads its hover pointer from the last mouse event instead of polling the OS cursor (on the root viewport `get_local_mouse_position` reads the OS pointer, which an event pushed through `Input.parse_input_event` never moves; a real mouse behaves the same); the composition and fill rule above. Left behind: the catalogue and viewer windows (`modules/sculpture_viewer`), the A/B/C variant switcher and its Left / Right key cycling (they would take the arrow keys from every Tab; smear A is fixed), the `?variant` / `?perf` / `?turn-seconds` levers (the performance-route fix of `d2faa30` only made `?perf` show the paintbox, which here is always shown), the perf telemetry, every JavaScriptBridge publish (now `state()`), `addons/stagehand`, and the no-longer-loaded pencil. The ~40 window-dragging lines are duplicated in `modules/sculpture_viewer/desktop.gd` on purpose (ticket #32; where stacking lives is #24's decision). The desktop sets `texture_filter` linear (the prototype's project default), which its children inherit; the paintbox sets nearest for itself as the prototype did. `drawing_surface.gd` still sets `Input.use_accumulated_input = false` on the first interactive surface's `_ready`, a global toggle every Tenant then shares. `face_viewport.msaa_2d = MSAA_4X` is a no-op on GLES3 (a warning on this host, not an error). modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:26:Layout (ticket #63). The native desktop is 2171x1185 px (the windows' rects in the picture plus a 24 px margin). From the Page's size S, `factor = min(S.x / 2171, S.y / 1185)` scales every window uniformly. The leftover on the other axis goes to the PostPet window: its rect runs to the middle column on the right and to the bottom margin. It is a raster, so it is drawn band by band at the uniform scale, and only a one-pixel column per band (a column with no horizontal step inside that band) and one flat row take up the extra width and height. The middle column and the phone anchor to the right edge, the chat window to the bottom edge. Every resize re-lays out (drags reset), and at any aspect the desktop spans the page within the margin.

modules/shell/MODULE.md:40:The fixed Tabs are strip indexes 0..6 forever: opened before any stub tab and never closable, so a stub tab closing never shifts them. Every Page starts hidden and frozen; the launch `grow_tab` on Collection is followed by `select_tab` on the strip's `tab_settled`. A selection kills any running fade, re-shows the Pages still on their way out (the strip hid them), moves the target on top of the PageStack, tweens `modulate.a` on all of them, and applies the freeze rule in the tween's callback. `boot_loader.tscn` is the project's main scene: the loading screen (four noise-driven dots and a bar drawn live into a SubViewport slightly smaller than the window, `tape_screen.gdshader` for a light colour bleed and edge halo), which on the Web mounts the game pack the page downloaded, loads `demo.tscn` under itself, shows every tab once so first clicks are instant, and lets the dots drift outward and fade. `demo.tscn` is the game: 1920x1080, resizable, stretch disabled (the CRT presentation below handles small windows); its registry maps `map` to the atlas module, `collection` to the owner's framed page (`assets/collection_frame/page.png`, a TextureRect built in `demo.gd`), `sketchbook`, `3d_viewer`, `video_player` to their ports, `playground` to the playground_page desktop, and `flowers` to flowers_page. The Tenant interfaces are the demo scene's only dependency beyond the strip; `shell.gd` itself knows no Tenant. Pixels: the strip's; the Shell draws nothing but white.

modules/sketchbook/MODULE.md:28:Frozen while hidden: the Shell hides the Page (`visible = false`, `process_mode DISABLED`); on hide the desktop hands the arrow back (the palette and the page both hide it) and parks the brush. Measured in the playtest: `_process` and `_input` counters stand still, a drag across the hidden page draws nothing and a click on the hidden arrow turns nothing, the finished-ink SubViewport stays at `UPDATE_ONCE` / `UPDATE_DISABLED` and the paper-turn face at `UPDATE_DISABLED`, and the frame's draw calls fall back to the white-page count (47 against 77 with the desktop shown); on show it resumes with the paint, the tray, the carried pigment, the spread and the windows exactly as left (pixel-identical).

modules/sketchbook/MODULE.md:36:`desktop.gd` is the desktop and the Tenant node; `paintbox.gd` (`paint_palette_prototype.gd`), `sketchbook_window.gd`, `drawing_surface.gd`, `freehand.gd` and `paper_turn.gd` are the prototype's scripts with their global `class_name`s dropped (the module preloads or loads them, so no other module can reach them by name) and their paths moved; `mixbox/` is Mixbox 2.0 unchanged. All come from `figma-ui-ux-qwen-pipeline` `prototype/painting-tool-mixbox` @ `d2faa30`; `PROVENANCE.md` lists every copied file with its hash, the records its pixels come from, and **the Mixbox licence: CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial only, notices kept; ticket #36 decides the road**. Changed from the prototype: the paintbox reads its hover pointer from the last mouse event instead of polling the OS cursor (on the root viewport `get_local_mouse_position` reads the OS pointer, which an event pushed through `Input.parse_input_event` never moves; a real mouse behaves the same); the composition and fill rule above. Left behind: the catalogue and viewer windows (`modules/sculpture_viewer`), the A/B/C variant switcher and its Left / Right key cycling (they would take the arrow keys from every Tab; smear A is fixed), the `?variant` / `?perf` / `?turn-seconds` levers (the performance-route fix of `d2faa30` only made `?perf` show the paintbox, which here is always shown), the perf telemetry, every JavaScriptBridge publish (now `state()`), `addons/stagehand`, and the no-longer-loaded pencil. The ~40 window-dragging lines are duplicated in `modules/sculpture_viewer/desktop.gd` on purpose (ticket #32; where stacking lives is #24's decision). The desktop sets `texture_filter` linear (the prototype's project default), which its children inherit; the paintbox sets nearest for itself as the prototype did. `drawing_surface.gd` still sets `Input.use_accumulated_input = false` on the first interactive surface's `_ready`, a global toggle every Tenant then shares. `face_viewport.msaa_2d = MSAA_4X` is a no-op on GLES3 (a warning on this host, not an error). No project setting changed.

modules/sketchbook/MODULE.md:38:The playtest (`scripts/playtest.sh sketchbook`, on `testing/harness_base.gd`) builds the Shell with this Tenant in the Sketchbook Tab and nothing in the other Tabs, on an X display at 1920x1080, drives it with real mouse events through `Input.parse_input_event` (tab clicks, well clicks, two tray drags, a page drag, the arrows, a title-bar drag, pointer moves) and reaches the desktop only through `ShellInterface.tenant_state`. `verify.py` re-hashes the screenshots, re-reads pixels and checks the logged states: lazy creation and page fill; the fill rule at 1920x1006, 1920x1000 and 1440x820 page sizes (uniform scale, paintbox art at native × s, the book taking the leftover, the windows' bounding box within the native margin by the rects and by the screenshot's non-white pixels); the brush on the rest at launch with a blue tip; a well loading pigment; A smeared, B dragged through it, the carried colour differing from both, and the tray's pixels showing a third colour where B crossed A; one stroke on the page in the carried pigment (by state and by the hue of the painted pixels); the brush off the rest while painting and back on it when idle, its tip in the carried pigment's hue; the turn in flight and landed on a blank spread 2, previous back to the paint; the title drag moving the window and its paint; frozen counters, nothing drawn or turned while hidden, quiet SubViewports and draw calls while hidden, identical pixels on resume, the 1440x900 re-fit and the restore (47 checks). Evidence of the accepted run is in `docs/evidence/sketchbook/`.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:26:Layout (ticket #63). The native desktop is 2171x1185 px (the windows' rects in the picture plus a 24 px margin). From the Page's size S, `factor = min(S.x / 2171, S.y / 1185)` scales every window uniformly. The leftover on the other axis goes to the PostPet window: its rect runs to the middle column on the right and to the bottom margin. It is a raster, so it is drawn band by band at the uniform scale, and only a one-pixel column per band (a column with no horizontal step inside that band) and one flat row take up the extra width and height. The middle column and the phone anchor to the right edge, the chat window to the bottom edge. Every resize re-lays out (drags reset), and at any aspect the desktop spans the page within the margin.

It reaches the desktop only through `ShellInterface.tenant_state`. `verify.py` re-reads the owner's layout picture and recomputes every window's place from the rects measured in it and the fill rule. It then compares each window's pixels in the screenshots with the picture at that place, with a shifted-crop control to prove the comparison discriminates. It also checks lazy creation, the drag and raise, body drag ignored, frozen counters and unchanged windows while hidden, identical pixels on resume, and at each size: windows at the rule's places, the desktop spanning the page on both axes within the margin, the main window never below native × factor, and pixels still matching (52 checks). modules/video_player/MODULE.md:16:The Page is the player's desktop, cut into the plate's two windows (owner correction #63, which asks for windows that fit the tab on both axes): the owner's Fly Through v7 screenshot supplies both, each with its own chrome — **Fly Through** (plate rect 64,54 1406x802: the video) and **Information** (282,888 938x658: the transport, the live title, Save, the eight tiles), the controls still cut from the same pixels and placed at their plate coordinates inside their window. The pair takes one uniform scale for the plate's pixels, from whichever arrangement scales larger with a 24 native px margin around and a 32 px gap between: **side by side** on a wide page (Fly Through left and larger, Information right; 0.792 at 1920x1006, 0.594 at 1440x845) or **stacked** on a tall one (Fly Through over Information, centred). The leftover goes to the windows so the pair spans the page on both axes: Fly Through grows by its straight frame runs (corners, caps and the "Fly Through" lettering fixed) with the video letterboxed in header light grey at the plate's aspect; Information grows in height by one plain white row of its body (its title and transport bar above and title, Save and tiles below stay fixed). Every resize lays the pair out again, dragged windows included. Each window drags by its own title bar and stops with 200 px of the bar across and all of its height inside the Page; with a title bar focused the arrows move that window. The side-by-side letterbox is deep at the owner's aspects (about 160 px of light grey above and below the video at 1920x1000) and Information's body is mostly white: the price of filling the tab with two fixed-aspect raster windows. Ticket #31's decisions hold: a tile click loads its mapped video at 0:00 and autoplays (tiles 1–5; 6–8 are visible and disabled); the controls are always shown — play/pause, the seek knob, the timer, the volume knob, mute, fullscreen, Save (this session) and the expand button; hover, pressed and settled play the Seedance frames on nine controls, then the source crop returns. Fullscreen fills the Page area (the video covers the Tenant, on top, taking the pointer), never the OS window; F or the control restores it. Keys while the Page is shown: `1`–`5`, Space, M, F, Left/Right (5 s); with the title bar focused the arrows move the viewer (Shift faster). The live title and timer use the bundled Liberation Sans; the strip stays font-free.

modules/shell/MODULE.md:26:`ShellInterface.create(registry)` returns a full-rect Control: a white ground, the PageStack filling the window above the bar, and the TabStrip along the **bottom** of the window (owner correction on map #23), fitted to the Shell's width (the owner's reference bar, 4180 source px across the window with the icon cluster at 65 percent; re-fitted on `resized`). It opens the seven fixed Tabs in launch order — `map`, `sketchbook`, `3d_viewer`, `video_player`, `collection`, `playground`, `flowers` — with Collection active. (Flowers joined after Playground on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. Six from 2026-09-14, when the owner folded the Phone Tab into the Playground desktop, #62; tab_strip's `layout.json` keeps the `phone` label file; the Shell no longer opens it.) The strip's stub keeps opening Blank Pages, which close as before; a fixed Tab has no close button and `close_tab` on it returns `shell.tab_fixed`.

modules/shell/MODULE.md:40:The fixed Tabs are strip indexes 0..6 forever: opened before any stub tab and never closable, so a stub tab closing never shifts them. Every Page starts hidden and frozen; the launch `grow_tab` on Collection is followed by `select_tab` on the strip's `tab_settled`. A selection kills any running fade, re-shows the Pages still on their way out (the strip hid them), moves the target on top of the PageStack, tweens `modulate.a` on all of them, and applies the freeze rule in the tween's callback. `boot_loader.tscn` is the project's main scene: the loading screen (four noise-driven dots and a bar drawn live into a SubViewport slightly smaller than the window, `tape_screen.gdshader` for a light colour bleed and edge halo), which on the Web mounts the game pack the page downloaded, loads `demo.tscn` under itself, shows every tab once so first clicks are instant, and lets the dots drift outward and fade. `demo.tscn` is the game: 1920x1080, resizable, stretch disabled (the CRT presentation below handles small windows); its registry maps `map` to the atlas module, `collection` to the owner's framed page (`assets/collection_frame/page.png`, a TextureRect built in `demo.gd`), `sketchbook`, `3d_viewer`, `video_player` to their ports, `playground` to the playground_page desktop, and `flowers` to flowers_page. The Tenant interfaces are the demo scene's only dependency beyond the strip; `shell.gd` itself knows no Tenant. Pixels: the strip's; the Shell draws nothing but white.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:46:With `show_fengshui` (on in the main demo) the Page follows the owner's layout picture of 2026-09-23 (`docs/evidence/playground-fengshui/layout-reference.png`): the Feng Shui window replaces PostPet on the left, the journal, WebSurfer and chat stack in the right column beside the Nokia, and options, filters and trade are hidden (in the picture they only peeked out from under other windows). The Feng Shui picture's title/menu/toolbar band and its element-panel band are drawn at the window's width; between them one row's side borders stretch. In the web build its client area carries the owner's Are.na profile, always in Are.na's light layout (`arena_embed.gd`: header, bio and the newest 24 blocks from the public API in two requests; the real page cannot be forced light inside an iframe), as HTML over the canvas, placed through the inverse of the CRT warp, laid out at 1200 px and scaled, cut away wherever a window above covers it, ignoring the pointer during a window drag and hidden with the Page. The desktop build leaves the client area white.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:14:Issue #173 restores the production Feng Shui desktop from `1a1fd69c`: journal, WebSurfer, phone and chat retain their overlapping draggable compositions. The four native browsing pages and shared data from #164 are now hosted inside the Feng Shui client opening. `show_page` forwards to that retained child. The earlier independent square-page option remains available to its isolated acceptance fixture; production no longer selects it. The external Are.na HTML overlay is replaced by these native pages.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:44:The playtest (`scripts/playtest.sh playground_page`, on `testing/harness_base.gd`) builds the Shell with this module in the Playground Tab and nothing in the other Tabs, on an X display at 1920x1080. It drives the desktop with real mouse and key events through `Input.parse_input_event`: the Playground tab, a title drag of the trade window, a body drag of options, the Map tab, a drag and a key while hidden, back, then window sizes giving 1920x1000 and 1440x820 pages, 1440x900 and 1920x1080. It reaches the desktop only through `ShellInterface.tenant_state`. `verify.py` re-reads the owner's layout picture and recomputes every window's place from the rects measured in it and the fill rule. It then compares each window's pixels in the screenshots with the picture at that place, with a shifted-crop control to prove the comparison discriminates. It also checks lazy creation, the drag and raise, body drag ignored, frozen counters and unchanged windows while hidden, identical pixels on resume, and at each size: windows at the rule's places, the desktop spanning the page on both axes within the margin, the main window never below native × factor, and pixels still matching (52 checks). Evidence of the accepted run is in `docs/evidence/playground/`.

Changed from the prototype: the paintbox reads its hover pointer from the last mouse event instead of polling the OS cursor (on the root viewport `get_local_mouse_position` reads the OS pointer, which an event pushed through `Input.parse_input_event` never moves; a real mouse behaves the same); the composition and fill rule above. modules/shell/MODULE.md:30:`registry` maps a fixed key to its Tenant: a Script whose `static create(deps) -> {ok, value: Control, error}` builds it, or a Callable with the same signature. The Tenant is created on the Tab's first show (`deps = {"key": key}`) and added to that Tab's Page, a plain white surface; a key with no entry keeps the white Page (`tenant_state` says `shell.tenant_missing`); a `create` that fails leaves it white and records `shell.tenant_failed`. The Shell's show/hide rule (ticket #24): the visible Page runs; once a fade has settled every hidden Page is `visible = false`, `process_mode DISABLED` (no `_process`, no input callbacks, no tweens, no video) with any focus inside it released, and resumes with its state intact from the moment its fade-in starts.

modules/shell/MODULE.md:42:The playtest (`scripts/playtest.sh shell`, on `testing/harness_base.gd`) builds the Shell with its own registry — the dummy tenant in four Tabs, a grey Callable-built tenant in `flowers` (so a cross-fade shows in pixels), nothing in `video_player` or `playground` — on an X display at 1920x1080, drives it with real mouse and key events through `Input.parse_input_event`, films the launch and two switches frame by frame, and `verify.py` re-hashes the screenshots, re-reads the film's pixels and checks the logged states, signals and tenant counters independently: seven fixed tabs in order along the bottom, the launch tab stub-sized then grown with its page shown only after the settle, `switch_settled` 0.55..1.0 s after mount, the pressed tint on the clicked tab within 100 ms and gone after 220 ms, the page blend through in-between greys, a switch settling 150..450 ms after the click, lazy creation, a hidden tenant's `_process` and input counters standing still and resuming, close refused by click and by call, the stub's blank page as the eighth tab, a resize to 1440x900 (48 checks). `playtest/browser_play.py` drives the Web export in headless Chrome. modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:26:Layout (ticket #63). The native desktop is 2171x1185 px (the windows' rects in the picture plus a 24 px margin). From the Page's size S, `factor = min(S.x / 2171, S.y / 1185)` scales every window uniformly. The leftover on the other axis goes to the PostPet window: its rect runs to the middle column on the right and to the bottom margin. It is a raster, so it is drawn band by band at the uniform scale, and only a one-pixel column per band (a column with no horizontal step inside that band) and one flat row take up the extra width and height. The middle column and the phone anchor to the right edge, the chat window to the bottom edge. Every resize re-lays out (drags reset), and at any aspect the desktop spans the page within the margin.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:44:The playtest (`scripts/playtest.sh playground_page`, on `testing/harness_base.gd`) builds the Shell with this module in the Playground Tab and nothing in the other Tabs, on an X display at 1920x1080. It drives the desktop with real mouse and key events through `Input.parse_input_event`: the Playground tab, a title drag of the trade window, a body drag of options, the Map tab, a drag and a key while hidden, back, then window sizes giving 1920x1000 and 1440x820 pages, 1440x900 and 1920x1080. It reaches the desktop only through `ShellInterface.tenant_state`. `verify.py` re-reads the owner's layout picture and recomputes every window's place from the rects measured in it and the fill rule. It then compares each window's pixels in the screenshots with the picture at that place, with a shifted-crop control to prove the comparison discriminates. It also checks lazy creation, the drag and raise, body drag ignored, frozen counters and unchanged windows while hidden, identical pixels on resume, and at each size: windows at the rule's places, the desktop spanning the page on both axes within the margin, the main window never below native × factor, and pixels still matching (52 checks). Evidence of the accepted run is in `docs/evidence/playground/`.

modules/shell/MODULE.md:40:The fixed Tabs are strip indexes 0..6 forever: opened before any stub tab and never closable, so a stub tab closing never shifts them. Every Page starts hidden and frozen; the launch `grow_tab` on Collection is followed by `select_tab` on the strip's `tab_settled`. A selection kills any running fade, re-shows the Pages still on their way out (the strip hid them), moves the target on top of the PageStack, tweens `modulate.a` on all of them, and applies the freeze rule in the tween's callback. `boot_loader.tscn` is the project's main scene: the loading screen (four noise-driven dots and a bar drawn live into a SubViewport slightly smaller than the window, `tape_screen.gdshader` for a light colour bleed and edge halo), which on the Web mounts the game pack the page downloaded, loads `demo.tscn` under itself, shows every tab once so first clicks are instant, and lets the dots drift outward and fade. `demo.tscn` is the game: 1920x1080, resizable, stretch disabled (the CRT presentation below handles small windows); its registry maps `map` to the atlas module, `collection` to the owner's framed page (`assets/collection_frame/page.png`, a TextureRect built in `demo.gd`), `sketchbook`, `3d_viewer`, `video_player` to their ports, `playground` to the playground_page desktop, and `flowers` to flowers_page. The Tenant interfaces are the demo scene's only dependency beyond the strip; `shell.gd` itself knows no Tenant. Pixels: the strip's; the Shell draws nothing but white.

modules/video_player/MODULE.md:16:The Page is the player's desktop, cut into the plate's two windows (owner correction #63, which asks for windows that fit the tab on both axes): the owner's Fly Through v7 screenshot supplies both, each with its own chrome — **Fly Through** (plate rect 64,54 1406x802: the video) and **Information** (282,888 938x658: the transport, the live title, Save, the eight tiles), the controls still cut from the same pixels and placed at their plate coordinates inside their window. The pair takes one uniform scale for the plate's pixels, from whichever arrangement scales larger with a 24 native px margin around and a 32 px gap between: **side by side** on a wide page (Fly Through left and larger, Information right; 0.792 at 1920x1006, 0.594 at 1440x845) or **stacked** on a tall one (Fly Through over Information, centred). The leftover goes to the windows so the pair spans the page on both axes: Fly Through grows by its straight frame runs (corners, caps and the "Fly Through" lettering fixed) with the video letterboxed in header light grey at the plate's aspect; Information grows in height by one plain white row of its body (its title and transport bar above and title, Save and tiles below stay fixed). Every resize lays the pair out again, dragged windows included. Each window drags by its own title bar and stops with 200 px of the bar across and all of its height inside the Page; with a title bar focused the arrows move that window. The side-by-side letterbox is deep at the owner's aspects (about 160 px of light grey above and below the video at 1920x1000) and Information's body is mostly white: the price of filling the tab with two fixed-aspect raster windows. Ticket #31's decisions hold: a tile click loads its mapped video at 0:00 and autoplays (tiles 1–5; 6–8 are visible and disabled); the controls are always shown — play/pause, the seek knob, the timer, the volume knob, mute, fullscreen, Save (this session) and the expand button; hover, pressed and settled play the Seedance frames on nine controls, then the source crop returns. Fullscreen fills the Page area (the video covers the Tenant, on top, taking the pointer), never the OS window; F or the control restores it. Keys while the Page is shown: `1`–`5`, Space, M, F, Left/Right (5 s); with the title bar focused the arrows move the viewer (Shift faster). The live title and timer use the bundled Liberation Sans; the strip stays font-free.

modules/atlas/MODULE.md:16:The Page is the atlas's desktop, the prototype's whole desktop as the owner corrected on map #23: the four supplied raster panels — minimap and calendar top-left, the itinerary under it, the chat bottom-left, the notification bubble bottom-right — around the map window, the prototype's frame pixels sliced around a `SubViewportContainer`. The composition is the prototype's 1950x1280 desktop (`PANEL_RECTS`, `FRAME_RECT`) filling the Page (owner correction #63): one uniform scale s = min(page / 1950x1280) for all the raster art, each panel kept at its native distance times s from the page edges nearest its centre (minimap, itinerary and chat to the left, chat and notification to the bottom, notification to the right), and the map window takes the leftover — its left edge beside the left panels and its bottom above the chat keep their native gaps, its top and right run to the page edge minus the desktop's native margin (`FRAME_FAR_GAP`), so it is never smaller than its native size times s and the page is full at any aspect. Every resize lays it out again, panels and window alike. Every window drags: a panel from anywhere on it, the map by its title bar; a press raises the pressed window to the top of the stack; drags clamp to the Page. The map window also resizes by its edges (300 px wide minimum), collapses by its left button and locks by its right one (the lock holds the frame only, as in the prototype). A wheel over a panel is swallowed, so the map beneath does not zoom. Inside, the zoomable atlas is the prototype's `atlas.gd` unchanged in behaviour: drag pans, the wheel zooms at the pointer (x1.18 a notch), double-click zooms in, Home/Esc reset, + and - zoom, arrows pan, F shows the region's full sheet; the HUD picks a region; close-city names appear past 1.8x in PixelMplus (`fonts/LICENSE.txt`), coastline tiles past 1.65x.

modules/video_player/MODULE.md:16:The Page is the player's desktop, cut into the plate's two windows (owner correction #63, which asks for windows that fit the tab on both axes): the owner's Fly Through v7 screenshot supplies both, each with its own chrome — **Fly Through** (plate rect 64,54 1406x802: the video) and **Information** (282,888 938x658: the transport, the live title, Save, the eight tiles), the controls still cut from the same pixels and placed at their plate coordinates inside their window. The pair takes one uniform scale for the plate's pixels, from whichever arrangement scales larger with a 24 native px margin around and a 32 px gap between: **side by side** on a wide page (Fly Through left and larger, Information right; 0.792 at 1920x1006, 0.594 at 1440x845) or **stacked** on a tall one (Fly Through over Information, centred). The leftover goes to the windows so the pair spans the page on both axes: Fly Through grows by its straight frame runs (corners, caps and the "Fly Through" lettering fixed) with the video letterboxed in header light grey at the plate's aspect; Information grows in height by one plain white row of its body (its title and transport bar above and title, Save and tiles below stay fixed). Every resize lays the pair out again, dragged windows included. Each window drags by its own title bar and stops with 200 px of the bar across and all of its height inside the Page; with a title bar focused the arrows move that window. The side-by-side letterbox is deep at the owner's aspects (about 160 px of light grey above and below the video at 1920x1000) and Information's body is mostly white: the price of filling the tab with two fixed-aspect raster windows. Ticket #31's decisions hold: a tile click loads its mapped video at 0:00 and autoplays (tiles 1–5; 6–8 are visible and disabled); the controls are always shown — play/pause, the seek knob, the timer, the volume knob, mute, fullscreen, Save (this session) and the expand button; hover, pressed and settled play the Seedance frames on nine controls, then the source crop returns. Fullscreen fills the Page area (the video covers the Tenant, on top, taking the pointer), never the OS window; F or the control restores it. Keys while the Page is shown: `1`–`5`, Space, M, F, Left/Right (5 s); with the title bar focused the arrows move the viewer (Shift faster). The live title and timer use the bundled Liberation Sans; the strip stays font-free.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:26:Layout (ticket #63). The native desktop is 2171x1185 px (the windows' rects in the picture plus a 24 px margin). From the Page's size S, `factor = min(S.x / 2171, S.y / 1185)` scales every window uniformly. The leftover on the other axis goes to the PostPet window: its rect runs to the middle column on the right and to the bottom margin. It is a raster, so it is drawn band by band at the uniform scale, and only a one-pixel column per band (a column with no horizontal step inside that band) and one flat row take up the extra width and height. The middle column and the phone anchor to the right edge, the chat window to the bottom edge. Every resize re-lays out (drags reset), and at any aspect the desktop spans the page within the margin.

modules/playground_page/MODULE.md:44:The playtest (`scripts/playtest.sh playground_page`, on `testing/harness_base.gd`) builds the Shell with this module in the Playground Tab and nothing in the other Tabs, on an X display at 1920x1080. It drives the desktop with real mouse and key events through `Input.parse_input_event`: the Playground tab, a title drag of the trade window, a body drag of options, the Map tab, a drag and a key while hidden, back, then window sizes giving 1920x1000 and 1440x820 pages, 1440x900 and 1920x1080. It reaches the desktop only through `ShellInterface.tenant_state`. `verify.py` re-reads the owner's layout picture and recomputes every window's place from the rects measured in it and the fill rule. It then compares each window's pixels in the screenshots with the picture at that place, with a shifted-crop control to prove the comparison discriminates. modules/tab_strip/MODULE.md:20:- Every stub-opened tab carries a close button (a Muse-drawn "x" in the toolbar's grey, `assets/icon_close.png`); clicking it folds the tab back into a stub over 0.3 s (contents fade, then the shape reverses the grow), removes the tab and its page, slides the remaining tabs and the stub to their new places over 0.2 s, and makes the left neighbour active. Every such tab can close, the last one too; with no tabs the stub sits at the first tab's place and opens a fresh one.

modules/tab_strip/MODULE.md:23:- Compact fixed-tab mode (the Shell, Issue #113) draws the owner-approved rebuilt taskbar from `assets/compact/` (sliced from Muse pass 16 by `assets/compact/provenance/`; `layout.json` there overrides the legacy geometry): star and Start, six 617 px tabs with their own icon and label (seven since Flowers, 2026-09-25: they share the row at 598 px, the IE7 shrink; the Flowers icon and label are one more Muse pass on the game's own pieces, `image-work/flowers-tab-label/`), the grey new-tab stub set lower, the tray on the tab axis. The tab middle tiles, so the dotted baseline repeats. The active tab's face switches at once to the stub's grey (0.911) and holds it, a static endpoint as the blue stills were; a click dips the tab at 0.85 grey; a stub-opened tab grows from the stub's grey, its close button fading in with the label, and carries the legacy page icon and Connecting.../Blank Page glyphs at 0.86 with their white matched to the face. The launch grow holds its tween until the first frame is drawn, so the pressed stub is always seen. `state()` reports the selected endpoint as `tint == 1`.

modules/tab_strip/MODULE.md:34:Geometry is in source pixels (bar 3135x161); `demo.gd` scales the strip to the window width. A tab is left slice + 1 px middle column stretched + right slice, all RGBA cutouts over the exact bar background (`bar_background.png` is the source bar with the tab and stub erased by stripe-aligned copies). Tab and stub cutouts follow the real outline pixels (face plus slant outline) and end just above the bar's bottom border, so the slants run unbroken down to the line and the line itself is the background's, one piece from end to end; the active tab covers it with a white opening into its page, as IE7 does. The bar's top and bottom borders in the three background sprites are flattened to one row profile (the Muse drawing's line wobbled in thickness). Tabs are drawn left-in-front and the stub behind all of them, as the source draws its stub behind the tab: a growing or folding tab is always behind its left neighbour, so the neighbour's corner never protrudes and the join is one line.

The ~40 window-dragging lines are duplicated in `modules/sculpture_viewer/desktop.gd` on purpose (ticket #32; where stacking lives is #24's decision). The desktop sets `texture_filter` linear (the prototype's project default), which its children inherit; the paintbox sets nearest for itself as the prototype did. `drawing_surface.gd` still sets `Input.use_accumulated_input = false` on the first interactive surface's `_ready`, a global toggle every Tenant then shares. `face_viewport.msaa_2d = MSAA_4X` is a no-op on GLES3 (a warning on this host, not an error). No project setting changed.
